events.title: Babies and Toddlers : Textiles Exhibition
events.description:
Take a nostalgic journey through the early years of childhood with our Babies & Toddlers exhibition.
Featuring beautiful garments, accessories, and treasured keepsakes, this charming display showcases how babies and toddlers were cared for, dressed, and celebrated across generations.
A highlight of the exhibition is a beautifully restored baby pram from the Museum’s collection, carefully brought back to life by our dedicated volunteers.
Discover the stories behind these special items, reminisce about days gone by, and share your own memories as you explore this heartwarming exhibition.

events.title: NAIDOC 2026 Exhibition: Fifty Years of Deadly
events.description: Curated by Margie Kennedy (COOEE Program Manager) this moving exhibition is a visual truth telling that honours the past, speaks to the present and empowers the future, through powerful images, cultural content and stories. Fifty Years of Deadly captures the strength of Elders, the vision of youth and the legacy that continues to shape their communities.

events.title: Our Communities Textiles Treasures : Textiles Exhibition
events.description:
Every textile has a story to tell, and every story helps preserve the history of the Redlands.
Community Textile Treasures celebrates a collection of special textile items connected to local families, memories, and milestones. From handmade garments and embroidered linens to treasured keepsakes and heirloom pieces, each item on display carries a unique story waiting to be shared.
Among the exhibition are pieces lovingly created for family members, treasured sewing projects, inherited textiles, and items that have become cherished reminders of people, places, and moments in time. Together, they create a rich tapestry of community history, craftsmanship, and personal connections.
As you explore the exhibition, discover the fascinating stories woven into every stitch and learn how these treasured objects help tell the story of the Redlands and the people who have called it home.
